items.title: ms_flow
items.text:
ms_flow runs the jobs of a scientific app in the app's own process: no broker, no daemon, no server. It works from a Qt app, a notebook or a script.

A task is what runs on one element. A job gives the elements, one by one, and says where the results go. The engine shares the elements out among the workers, keeps a journal of what is done, and continues a job that was cut short without running again what it had done.

items.title: Install
items.text:
pip install ms_flow
pip install "ms_flow[ray]"   # to run on the machines of a network with Ray

The package requires Python 3.12 or newer. The desktop widgets (projects, job monitor) are in the separate ms_components package.

items.title: First use
items.text:
Tasks and jobs live in a module the workers can import, never in __main__.

workers.py:

from sqlmodel import Field, SQLModel

from ms_flow import job, table_sink, task


class Result(SQLModel, table=True):      # the project creates this table when it opens
    __tablename__ = "results"
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    value: int
    double_value: int


@task()
def double_value(value: int) -> dict:
    return {"value": value, "double_value": 2 * value}


@job(task=double_value, output=table_sink("results", columns=("value", "double_value")))
def double_values(params, project):
    yield from range(1000)

run.py:

from ms_flow import Workspace
from workers import Result, double_values

ms = Workspace(app_id="demo")
try:
    ms.create_or_open_project(name="demo", folder="./demo_project", activate=True)
    job_id = ms.submit(double_values)        # on the pool of processes of this machine
    print(ms.engine.wait(job_id).status)     # completed
    print(ms.project_db.count(Result))       # 1000
finally:
    ms.shutdown()

def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    app_id: str,
    host_namespace: str | None = None,
    project_resources=None,
    app_settings=None,
):
    self.app_id = str(app_id).strip()
    if not self.app_id:
        raise ValueError("Workspace requires a non-empty app_id.")
    self.host_namespace = str(host_namespace or "").strip() or self.app_id
    self.settings_manager = SettingsManager()
    legacy_specs = coerce_app_setting_specs(app_settings)
    if legacy_specs:
        self.settings_manager.register_app_settings(self.app_id, legacy_specs)
    logging_cfg = self.settings_manager.settings.logging
    self.logging_manager = LoggingManager(
        global_log_dir=self.settings_manager.settings.projects_db.parent / "logs",
        max_bytes=logging_cfg.max_file_size_mb * 1024 * 1024,
        backup_count=logging_cfg.backup_count,
        retention_days=logging_cfg.retention_days,
        queue_size=logging_cfg.queue_size,
        app_level=logging_cfg.app_level,
        executor_level=logging_cfg.executor_level,
        project_level=logging_cfg.project_level,
        console_level=logging_cfg.console_level,
        root_namespace=self.host_namespace,
    )
    self.logging_manager.start()
    self.app_logger = self.logging_manager.get_app_logger("core")

    self._master_db_path = self.settings_manager.settings.projects_db

    self.master_db = MasterDB(self._master_db_path)
    self.project_manager = ProjectManager(self.master_db, app_id_filter=self.app_id)
    if self.settings_manager.settings.general.prune_missing_projects:
        pruned = self.project_manager.repository.delete_missing_projects()
        if pruned:
            self.app_logger.info("Pruned %d registry entries with missing project folders.", pruned)
    self._project_resource_contract = ProjectResourceContract(
        app_id=self.app_id,
        specs=coerce_project_resource_specs(project_resources),
    )

    self._runtime_state = ProjectRuntimeState()
    self._engine = self._flow = None  # see `Workspace.engine` and `Workspace.submit`
    # see `Workspace.activate`: who put the pool of this machine aside, who is starting, one at a time
    self._aside, self._starting, self._activation = None, set(), threading.Lock()
    self.project_logger = None
    self._advanced = WorkspaceAdvancedAccess(self)

def open_project(
    self,
    project_id: str | UUID,
    *,
    cancel_running_tasks_on_switch: bool = True,
    touch_master: bool = True,
    extra_dirs: list[str] | None = None,
) -> ProjectContext:
    normalized_id = self._normalize_id(project_id)
    self._validate_project_access(normalized_id)

    if self.active_context:
        if self.active_context.id == normalized_id:
            return self.active_context
        self.close_project(cancel_running_tasks=cancel_running_tasks_on_switch)

    context = self.project_manager.load_project_by_id(
        normalized_id,
        sm=self.settings_manager,
        extra_dirs=self._merge_project_dirs(extra_dirs),
    )
    self._activate_context(context, touch_master=touch_master)
    self.app_logger.info(
        "Project activated: id=%s name=%s",
        context.id,
        context.name,
        extra={"project_id": str(context.id)},
    )
    return context

def create_project(
    self,
    name: str,
    folder: Path | str,
    description: str = "",
    tags: list[str] | None = None,
    base_settings: SettingsProfile = "global",
    scope: str = "full",
    activate: bool = True,
    extra_dirs: list[str] | None = None,
) -> ProjectContext:
    folder = Path(folder).expanduser().resolve()
    normalized_scope = str(scope).strip()
    effective_scope = normalized_scope or "full"
    if effective_scope == "full":
        effective_scope = self.app_id
    context = self.project_manager.create_project(
        name=name,
        folder=folder,
        sm=self.settings_manager,
        base=base_settings,
        description=description,
        scope=effective_scope,
        app_id=self.app_id,
        tags=tags,
        extra_dirs=self._merge_project_dirs(extra_dirs),
    )
    if not activate:
        return context

    if self.active_context and self.active_context.id != context.id:
        self.close_project(cancel_running_tasks=True)
    self._activate_context(context, touch_master=True)
    self.app_logger.info(
        "Project created and activated: id=%s name=%s",
        context.id,
        context.name,
        extra={"project_id": str(context.id)},
    )
    return context

def create_or_open_project(
    self,
    *,
    name: str,
    folder: Path | str,
    description: str = "",
    tags: list[str] | None = None,
    base_settings: SettingsProfile = "global",
    scope: str = "full",
    cancel_running_tasks_on_switch: bool = True,
    activate: bool = True,
    extra_dirs: list[str] | None = None,
) -> ProjectContext:
    folder_path = Path(folder).expanduser().resolve()
    existing_at_path = self.project_manager.find_project_global(folder=folder_path)
    if existing_at_path is not None:
        existing_app_id = (existing_at_path.app_id or "").strip()
        if existing_app_id != self.app_id:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Path '{folder_path}' already belongs to project '{existing_at_path.name}' "
                f"of app_id='{existing_app_id or '<empty>'}'."
            )
        if activate:
            return self.open_project(
                existing_at_path.id,
                cancel_running_tasks_on_switch=cancel_running_tasks_on_switch,
                touch_master=True,
                extra_dirs=self._merge_project_dirs(extra_dirs),
            )
        return self.project_manager.load_project(
            project=existing_at_path,
            sm=self.settings_manager,
            extra_dirs=self._merge_project_dirs(extra_dirs),
        )
    existing = self.project_manager.find_project(name=name)
    if existing is not None:
        if activate:
            return self.open_project(
                existing.id,
                cancel_running_tasks_on_switch=cancel_running_tasks_on_switch,
                touch_master=True,
                extra_dirs=self._merge_project_dirs(extra_dirs),
            )
        return self.project_manager.load_project(
            project=existing,
            sm=self.settings_manager,
            extra_dirs=self._merge_project_dirs(extra_dirs),
        )
    return self.create_project(
        name=name,
        folder=folder_path,
        description=description,
        tags=tags,
        base_settings=base_settings,
        scope=scope,
        activate=activate,
        extra_dirs=self._merge_project_dirs(extra_dirs),
    )

close_project(cancel_running_tasks: bool = True)

Close the active project. Its jobs that have not ended are interrupted, not lost: submitted again under the same key in a later session, each continues where it stopped.

With cancel_running_tasks=False, raises instead when one is still going on.

Source code in src/ms_flow/_api_impl/project_runtime.py 
def close_project(self, cancel_running_tasks: bool = True):
    """Close the active project. Its jobs that have not ended are interrupted, not lost:
    submitted again under the same key in a later session, each continues where it stopped.

    With `cancel_running_tasks=False`, raises instead when one is still going on.
    """
    if not self.active_context:
        self.settings_manager.clear_project()
        self.logging_manager.clear_project_logging()
        return

    context = self.active_context
    if cancel_running_tasks:
        self._cancel_project_tasks(context.id)
    elif self.get_project_activity()["jobs_active"]:
        raise RuntimeError("The project cannot be closed while active jobs remain.")

    self.project_manager.close_project(context)
    self._close_project_runtime()
    self.settings_manager.clear_project()
    self.app_logger.info(
        "Project closed: id=%s name=%s",
        context.id,
        context.name,
        extra={"project_id": str(context.id)},
    )

def get_project_activity(self, project_id: str | UUID | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What is still going on in a project: its jobs that have not ended, and the external
    tasks registered with `register_task_canceller`. Only the active project has any.
    """
    context = self.active_context
    mine = context is not None and (project_id is None or context.id == self._normalize_id(project_id))
    # ponytail: every recorded job of the engine counts, as the project's journal is the
    # only one this facade attaches.
    jobs = [
        job
        for job in (self._engine.jobs() if mine and self._flow is not None else ())
        if job.key is not None and job.status in ("waiting", "running")
    ]
    cancellers = len(self._runtime_state.active_project.task_cancellers) if mine else 0
    active = bool(jobs or cancellers)
    return {
        "project_id": str(project_id or context.id) if project_id or context else None,
        "active": active,
        "can_switch_project": not active,
        "jobs_active": len(jobs),
        "job_ids": [job.id for job in jobs],
        "statuses": sorted({job.status for job in jobs}),
        "external_cancellers": cancellers,
    }

def delete_projects(self, project_ids: list[str | UUID], delete_files: bool = True):
    normalized_ids = []
    for project_id in project_ids:
        try:
            normalized_ids.append(self._normalize_id(project_id))
        except ValueError:
            continue

    if not normalized_ids:
        return

    if self.active_context and self.active_context.id in normalized_ids:
        self.close_project()

    self.project_manager.delete_projects(normalized_ids, delete_files=delete_files)
    self.app_logger.info("Projects deleted: count=%s delete_files=%s", len(normalized_ids), delete_files)

def executors(self) -> list[dict]:
    """One row for each executor kept: `name`, `kind`, `hosts`, `default`, and `state`:
    `on`, `starting`, `off`, or `blocked` when it is off and not to be started now, with
    `why`. Safe to poll."""
    settings, active = self.settings_manager.settings, self._active()
    rows = []
    for name, config in settings.executors.items():
        why = "" if name in active or name in self._starting else blocked(name, settings, active)

activate(name: str, on_line=None) -> None

Start the executor kept as name, which takes jobs under that name from then on.

Refused with ValueError while another active one has one of its machines or is a Ray too (see blocked). A Ray that takes this machine puts the pool of it aside until it is deactivated, so the pool must have no job that has not ended. A host that is not reached or not prepared raises, and leaves everything as it was. on_line hears what is done on a host that is being prepared. It waits for its hosts: not from a thread that cannot.

def activate(self, name: str, on_line=None) -> None:
    """Start the executor kept as `name`, which takes jobs under that name from then on.

    Refused with `ValueError` while another active one has one of its machines or is a Ray
    too (see `blocked`). A Ray that takes this machine puts the pool of it aside until it
    is deactivated, so the pool must have no job that has not ended. A host that is not
    reached or not prepared raises, and leaves everything as it was. `on_line` hears what
    is done on a host that is being prepared. It waits for its hosts: not from a thread
    that cannot.
    """
    settings, engine = self.settings_manager.settings, self.engine
    if name not in settings.executors:
        raise ValueError(f"no executor is kept as `{name}`")
    self._starting.add(name)
    try:
        with self._activation:
            if name in engine._executors:
                return
            why = blocked(name, settings, self._active())
            if why:
                raise ValueError(f"`{name}` is not started: {why}")
            config = settings.executors[name]
            aside = config.kind == "ray" and "local" in config.hosts and "local" in engine._executors
            if aside:
                try:
                    engine.unregister("local")
                except ValueError:
                    raise ValueError(f"`{name}` takes this machine, and its pool has jobs that have not ended") from None
            try:
                host_env = self.host_env and (lambda address, busy: self.host_env(address, busy, on_line))
                executor = build_executor(name, settings, host_env)
                if executor is None:
                    raise RuntimeError(_LOGIN_NODE)
                engine.register(name, executor)
            except BaseException:
                if aside:
                    self._local_back()
                raise
            if aside:
                self._aside = name
    finally:
        self._starting.discard(name)

def move(self, key: str, executor: str, **options) -> int:
    """Continue on `executor` the job recorded under `key`: `resume`, for one that may be running.
    A job this session runs is canceled first and waited for, so not from a thread that cannot
    wait: what its tasks in flight had done is done again there."""
    self.origin(key)  # nothing is canceled for a job that cannot be submitted again,
    self._ready(executor)  # or that has nowhere to go
    for job in self._engine.jobs():
        if job.key == key and job.finished_at is None:
            self._engine.cancel(job.id)
            self._engine.wait(job.id)
    return self.resume(key, executor=executor, **options)

items.text:
jobs(limit: int | None = None) -> list

The jobs of the active project, oldest first; with limit, the last ones.

What a monitor shows: every job on record in the project's journal, the ones of earlier sessions too, each as the engine has it now when it ran it in this session. Reads the journal without owning it and never builds the engine, so it is safe to poll.

Source code in src/ms_flow/_api_impl/job_api.py 
def jobs(self, limit: int | None = None) -> list:
    """The jobs of the active project, oldest first; with `limit`, the last ones.

    What a monitor shows: every job on record in the project's journal, the ones of earlier
    sessions too, each as the engine has it now when it ran it in this session. Reads the
    journal without owning it and never builds the engine, so it is safe to poll.
    """
    project = self._runtime_state.active_project
    if project is None:
        return []
    from ms_flow.engine import JobSnapshot
    from ms_flow.engine.journal import recorded

    live = {(job.key, job.started_at): job for job in (self._engine.jobs() if self._flow is not None else ())}
    # ponytail: a job of a process that died reads as running until this session's first
    # submit opens the journal, which is what marks it interrupted.
    listed = [live.pop((row["job_id"], row["started_at"]), None)
              or JobSnapshot(None, row["name"], row["status"], row["total"], row["done"], row["failed"], 0,
                             row["error"], 0, row["started_at"], row["finished_at"], row["job_id"], 0,
                             min(1.0, (row["done"] + row["failed"]) / row["total"]) if row["total"] else None,
                             executor=_spec_executor(row["spec"]))
              for row in recorded(project.context.path / "executor.db", limit)]
    # One just submitted is not in the file until the journal's next write. Only the active
    # project has jobs that have not ended: closing a project interrupts its own.
    return listed + [job for job in live.values() if job.finished_at is None]

def job(*, task, name: str = "", params_model=None, output=None, reads=(), finalize=None):
    """Mark a function `(params, project)` as a job: the elements it gives go to `task`, the results to `output`.

    It is a generator, or returns whatever can be read one element at a time: `ms_flow.query.Rows`
    for the rows of a table, which also gives the job its total and the table it reads.
    `output` is a `table_sink` (the task returns rows) or a `graph_sink` (it returns
    `{node: rows}`; a `$ref` names its row within what the element returned), a `file_sink`
    (it returns text or bytes, written as they come, or anything else, written as JSON) or a
    function `(params, project)` that returns the job's own writer (see the module's note).
    `reads` is the tables the source reads, besides the ones it says itself: the job waits for
    the jobs writing them.
    `finalize(params, project, snapshot)` is called once the job has ended, however it ended:
    what there is to tidy up when it failed or was canceled.
    """
    if not hasattr(task, "__task__"):
        raise TypeError(f"{task!r} is not a task: decorate it with @task(...)")
    if output is not None and not (hasattr(output, "table") or hasattr(output, "fmt") or callable(output)):
        raise TypeError("output is a table_sink, a graph_sink, a file_sink or a function that returns a writer")

    def mark(source):
        source.__job__ = {"task": task, "name": name or source.__name__, "params_model": params_model,
                          "output": output, "reads": frozenset(reads), "finalize": finalize}
        return source
    return mark

def content_key(payload) -> bytes:
    """16 bytes that identify a chunk by what it carries, the same in every run.

    Equal keys mean equal payloads. The reverse is not promised: a payload built another
    way (dict order, a set) gets another key, so on resume it is repeated, never skipped.
    """
    try:
        data = pickle.dumps(payload, protocol=4)
    except Exception:
        return uuid.uuid4().bytes  # nothing to recognise it by in another run
    return hashlib.blake2b(data, digest_size=16).digest()

def table_sink(
    table: str = "",
    *,
    model: type[SQLModel] | None = None,
    columns: Iterable[str] = (),
    write_mode: str = "bulk",
    conflict_keys: Iterable[str] = (),
    validate_model: bool = False,
    db_role: str = "project",
    db_path: str | Path = "",
    schema: str = "",
    meta: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
) -> DbOutputSpec:
    """Simple helper to persist results into a SQLite table.

    `write_mode="upsert"` updates existing rows via `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT
    (conflict_keys) DO UPDATE`. Each emitted row only updates the columns it carries
    (SET is built per payload), so it needs `model` and `conflict_keys` to be the PK
    or a UNIQUE constraint of the table.
    """
    resolved_table = _model_table_name(model) if model is not None else str(table)
    # For upsert we keep explicit columns when given so the SET clause is scoped;
    # otherwise default to the model's writable columns.
    if columns:
        resolved_columns: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(str(col) for col in columns)
    elif model is not None:
        resolved_columns = _model_output_columns(model)
        if str(write_mode or "").strip().lower() == "upsert":
            resolved_columns = _with_conflict_keys(resolved_columns, (str(key) for key in conflict_keys))
    else:
        resolved_columns = ()
    return DbOutputSpec(
        table=resolved_table,
        columns=resolved_columns,
        model_path=_model_path(model) if model is not None else "",
        write_mode=str(write_mode or "bulk"),
        conflict_keys=tuple(str(key) for key in conflict_keys),
        validate_model=bool(validate_model),
        db_role=str(db_role or "project"),
        db_path=str(db_path or ""),
        schema=str(schema or ""),
        meta=dict(meta or {}),
    )

db_pages(source: Any, spec: QuerySpec, *, key: str = 'id', page_size: int = 500) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]

The same rows as db_stream, but in keyset pages.

Each page is its own short read (WHERE key > last ORDER BY key LIMIT n) instead of a single cursor held open for the whole feed. Feeding a million-ligand screen takes hours, and a read snapshot held open that long prevents SQLite from checkpointing the WAL: project.db-wal grows without bound while the job itself writes its results.

Without a usable key (raw SQL, offset, or an order other than key) no keyset is possible: it falls back to db_stream, which returns exactly the same rows.

def db_pages(
    source: Any,
    spec: QuerySpec,
    *,
    key: str = "id",
    page_size: int = 500,
) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
    """The same rows as `db_stream`, but in keyset pages.

    Each page is its own short read (`WHERE key > last ORDER BY key LIMIT n`) instead of a single
    cursor held open for the whole feed. Feeding a million-ligand screen takes hours, and a read
    snapshot held open that long prevents SQLite from checkpointing the WAL: `project.db-wal`
    grows without bound while the job itself writes its results.

    Without a usable key (raw SQL, `offset`, or an order other than `key`) no keyset is possible:
    it falls back to `db_stream`, which returns exactly the same rows.
    """
    key_name = str(key or "").strip()
    pageable = (
        bool(spec.table)
        and bool(key_name)
        and not spec.offset
        and (not spec.fields or key_name in spec.fields)
        and (not spec.order or tuple(spec.order) == (key_name,))
    )
    if not pageable:
        yield from db_stream(source, spec, batch_size=page_size)
        return

    backend = resolve_project_store(source)
    size = max(1, int(page_size))
    remaining = None if spec.limit is None else int(spec.limit)
    cursor: Any = None
    while remaining is None or remaining > 0:
        take = size if remaining is None else min(size, remaining)
        filters = dict(spec.filters)
        if cursor is not None:
            filters[f"{key_name}__gt"] = cursor
        page = replace(spec, filters=filters, order=(key_name,), limit=take, offset=0)
        rows = backend.read_rows(_as_project_read_query(page))
        if not rows:
            return
        yield from rows
        if len(rows) < take:
            return
        cursor = rows[-1].get(key_name)
        if cursor is None:
            return  # no cursor, no progress; stopping beats repeating the page forever
        if remaining is not None:
            remaining -= len(rows)

def __init__(self, cpus: int | None = None, gpus: int = 0, mem_mb: int | None = None, state_dir=None):
    """`mem_mb` is the memory budget for chunks; by default physical RAM minus a reserve.

    With `state_dir`, this is the one engine that shares out the local machine: it owns
    `engine.lock` there, and a second process gets `Busy` instead of the same CPUs.
    """
    self._lock = own(Path(state_dir) / "engine.lock") if state_dir is not None else None
    self.tokens = Tokens(cpus or usable_cpus(), gpus,
                         memory_budget_mb() if mem_mb is None else mem_mb)
    self._executors: dict[str, _Slot] = {}
    self._journals: dict[str, Journal] = {}
    self._jobs: dict[int, _Job] = {}  # the ones that have not ended
    self._ended: dict[int, JobSnapshot] = {}  # the last _REMEMBERED that have, oldest first
    self._active: list[_Job] = []  # running jobs, by priority and then arrival
    self._waiting: list[_Job] = []
    self._ids = itertools.count(1)
    self._timers: list = []  # (when, tie-break, fn, args), a heap; the loop's own
    self._ticks = itertools.count()
    self._events: queue.SimpleQueue = queue.SimpleQueue()  # into the loop
    self._deliveries: queue.SimpleQueue = queue.SimpleQueue()  # user callbacks, out of the loop
    self._closed = False
    self._threads = [threading.Thread(target=self._loop, name="msflow-engine", daemon=True),
                     threading.Thread(target=self._deliver, name="msflow-delivery", daemon=True)]
    for thread in self._threads:
        thread.start()

def unregister(self, name: str) -> None:
    """Shut down the executor registered as `name`, if there is one.

    Raises `ValueError` while a job submitted to it has not ended: an executor changes
    between jobs, never under one.
    """
    slot = self._executors.get(name)
    if slot is None:
        return
    # ponytail: whoever changes executors is whoever submits; a submit from another thread
    # at this very moment could still land on the one going away.
    if any(job.slot is slot for job in list(self._jobs.values())):
        raise ValueError(f"executor {name!r} has jobs that have not ended")
    self._executors = {key: kept for key, kept in self._executors.items() if key != name}
    slot.impl.shutdown()

def detach(self, name: str) -> None:
    """Interrupt the jobs recorded in this journal, wait until it is written and close it."""
    if self._closed:
        return
    journal = self._journals[name]
    self._journals = {k: v for k, v in self._journals.items() if k != name}
    told = threading.Event()
    self._events.put((self._on_detach, journal, told))
    told.wait()
    told.clear()
    self._events.put((told.set,))  # behind the loop taking note of what those callbacks took
    told.wait()
    journal.close()

           window: int | None = None, max_cpu: float | None = None, priority: int = 0,
           total: int | None = None, name: str = "", journal: str | None = None, key: str | None = None,
           after=(), retries: int = 0, retry_wait: float = 1.0, timeout: float | None = None,
           batch: int | None = None, batched: bool = False, progress: bool | None = None, origin=None,
           label=None, thread: bool = False,
           on_result=None, on_results=None, on_error=None, on_finish=None, on_terminal=None) -> int:
    """Run `fn(payload)` for every payload in `chunks` on `executor`. Returns the job id.

    `cpu`, `gpu` and `mem_mb` are what one chunk needs; a dict payload may say otherwise
    for itself with `_cpu_required`, `_gpu_required` and `_mem_mb`, which `fn` never sees.
    `max_cpu` caps the job as a whole; a chunk above the cap runs alone in its job.
    `chunks` is read on its own thread. `window` is how many chunks may be between dispatch
    and delivered result, and how many more may be read ahead.
    Chunks that take well under a task's worth of time travel several to a task where the
    executor allows it; each still succeeds, fails and is recorded on its own. Left to
    itself the window grows with them, since such chunks are small by construction.
    `batch` settles it instead: that many chunks to a task, fewer only in the last one and
    where chunks with different needs meet. With `batched`, `fn` takes the list of payloads
    of a task and returns one result for each, in order; if it raises, all of them failed.
    A chunk's key is `content_key(payload)`, or the `_key` of a dict payload.
    `on_result(key, result)`, `on_error(key, error)` and `on_terminal(snapshot)` run on
    the delivery thread, in order; a chunk counts as done once `on_result` returns.
    `on_results(pairs)` takes its place for whoever writes results somewhere: it gets every
    `(key, result)` of the job that is waiting, up to `_DELIVER_MAX`, and all of them count as
    done once it returns. When it raises, each pair is offered again alone and only the ones
    that raise again fail, so it must leave nothing behind when it raises: one transaction.
    `on_finish()` is the job's last word: called once every chunk has ended, on the delivery
    thread, before the job counts as completed and the jobs after it start. If it raises, the
    job fails with that error. A job that failed, was canceled or interrupted never gets there.
    `chunks` may know more than how to be read. With `remaining()`, how many chunks it has yet
    to give, the job has a total while it runs: counted at its first chunk and every
    `_RECOUNT` seconds after, exact once the source is read. With `open(state)`, it is called
    before the first read and what it returns (JSON) is kept with the job in its journal and
    passed back as `state` when the job continues; `state` is None the first time.
    `progress` says whether the tasks of the job are watched, for `JobSnapshot.progress` to
    count how far the running chunks are and not only the ones that ended (see
    `executors.report`). By default every task is on an executor that watches for nothing (the
    process pool); on another, a task of several chunks, and a task of one when the job has at
    most two for each worker.
    `thread` says that `fn` spends its time waiting for a program it starts, not in Python:
    an executor that keeps a worker for each task and can spare it (the process pool) runs it
    on a thread of one process it keeps for all of them, so no worker holds memory for it.
    `label` is what a chunk goes by in `tasks` and in a failure, in place of a short repr of
    its payload: a template the payload fills (`"dock-R{receptor}-L{ligand}"`, the keys of a
    dict payload) or a function `(payload)` that returns the text. It runs here, never in a
    worker, and only for a chunk that is shown.
    `journal` names an attached journal; without it nothing about the job reaches the disk.
    `key` is what the job is called there. Submitting an interrupted or canceled job again
    under its key continues it: the chunks it had done are recognised by their own keys and
    not run again. `discard` is how such a job is given up instead.
    `origin` is whatever whoever submits wants kept with the job there (JSON): `recorded`
    gives it back in `spec`.
    `after` is the ids of the jobs that must end first; `chunks` is not read until they do,
    and the job fails if one of them fails, is canceled or is interrupted.
    A chunk that fails runs again up to `retries` times, `retry_wait` seconds after the first
    failure and twice as long after each one that follows. Failing is raising, running past
    `timeout` seconds or killing its worker; falling with somebody else's worker is not, and
    costs the chunk nothing. `on_error` hears of a chunk only once it has failed for good.
    `timeout` needs an executor that can stop a running chunk; the process pool stops all
    of its chunks to stop one, and the others start again.
    """
    if self._closed:
        raise RuntimeError("engine is closed")
    slot = self._executors.get(executor)
    if slot is None:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown executor {executor!r}; registered: {sorted(self._executors)}")
    if on_result is not None and on_results is not None:
        raise ValueError("on_result or on_results, not both")
    batch = batch or getattr(slot.impl, "batch", None)
    if (batch or batched) and not slot.packs:
        raise ValueError(f"executor {executor!r} takes one chunk to a task")
    if timeout is not None and not slot.kills:
        raise ValueError(f"executor {executor!r} cannot stop a running chunk, so its chunks cannot have a timeout")
    job = _Job()
    job.executor = executor
    job.journal = job.n = job.uid = job.spec = job.skip = job.source = job.key = None
    job.retries, job.retry_wait, job.timeout, job.retried = retries, retry_wait, timeout, 0
    job.after = [self._jobs.get(job_id) or self._ended[job_id] for job_id in after]
    if journal is not None:
        job.journal = self._journals.get(journal)
        if job.journal is None or job.journal.failed:
            raise ValueError(f"no usable journal {journal!r}; attached: {sorted(self._journals)}")
        job.uid, job.key = key or uuid.uuid4().hex, key  # `key`: what another run can ask for it by
        job.spec = json.dumps({
            "executor": executor, "fn": f"{getattr(fn, '__module__', '')}:{getattr(fn, '__qualname__', repr(fn))}",
            "cpu": cpu, "gpu": gpu, "mem_mb": mem_mb, "window": window, "max_cpu": max_cpu, "priority": priority,
            "retries": retries, "retry_wait": retry_wait, "timeout": timeout, "batch": batch, "origin": origin})
    job.cost = (cpu, gpu, mem_mb) if slot.impl.uses_tokens else None
    job.needs = (cpu, gpu, mem_mb)
    if job.cost is not None and not self.tokens.ever_fits(job.cost):
        raise ValueError(f"a chunk needing (cpu, gpu, mem_mb)={job.cost} can never run: "
                         f"the engine has {self.tokens.total}")
    job.id, job.name, job.slot, job.fn, job.max_cpu = next(self._ids), name, slot, fn, max_cpu
    job.batch, job.batched, job.fine, job.label = batch or 0, batched, progress, label
    job.thread = thread and slot.threads
    job.window = max(window or 2 * slot.impl.capacity * (batch or 1), batch or 1)
    job.pace, job.pack, job.elastic = 0.0, batch or 1, window is None
    job.priority, job.on_result, job.on_error, job.on_terminal = priority, on_result, on_error, on_terminal
    job.on_results, job.on_finish, job.finishing = on_results, on_finish, False
    job.status, job.chunks = WAITING if job.after else RUNNING, chunks
    job.total = len(chunks) if total is None and hasattr(chunks, "__len__") else total
    job.done = job.failed = job.open = job.seq = job.peak_mem_mb = 0
    job.states = bytearray()  # a byte per chunk the source gave, in its order; see `chunk_states`
    if key is not None and job.journal is not None:
        resumed = job.journal.claim(key)
        if resumed is not None:
            job.n, job.skip, job.source = resumed  # `skip`: how many chunks it had done
            job.done = job.skip
            # ponytail: what it had done goes first, wherever the source has it.
            job.states = bytearray([DONE_CHUNK]) * job.skip
    job.flying, job.cpu_used, job.fatal, job.error = set(), 0, None, None
    job.ready, job.room, job.hungry, job.fed_all = deque(), threading.Event(), False, False
    job.started_at, job.finished_at, job.finished = time.time(), None, threading.Event()
    self._jobs[job.id] = job
    self._events.put((self._on_submit, job))
    return job.id

items.title: tasks
items.text:
tasks(job_id: int) -> list[TaskSnapshot]

The tasks of the job that are with its executor now, the oldest first: what a monitor unfolds under a running job. At most a window of them, and none once the job ended.

Source code in src/ms_flow/engine/engine.py 
def tasks(self, job_id: int) -> list[TaskSnapshot]:
    """The tasks of the job that are with its executor now, the oldest first: what a monitor
    unfolds under a running job. At most a window of them, and none once the job ended."""
    job = self._jobs.get(job_id)
    flying = sorted(tuple(job.flying), key=lambda chunk: chunk.started) if job is not None else ()
    told = job.slot.impl.progress(job.id) if flying and job.slot.tells else {}
    at = job.slot.impl.hosts() if flying and job.slot.places else {}
    now, tasks = time.perf_counter(), []
    for chunk in flying:
        pack, said = chunk.pack, told.get(chunk)  # `pack` once: the loop empties it as the task ends
        n = len(pack) if pack else 1
        tasks.append(TaskSnapshot(_called(job, chunk.payload), n, chunk.attempt, now - chunk.started,
                                  None if said is None else min(1.0, said / n), at.get(chunk)))
    return tasks

A byte per chunk of the job, in the order its source gave them: PENDING_CHUNK, RUNNING_CHUNK (with its executor, or its result on the way), DONE_CHUNK or FAILED_CHUNK. Chunks the source has not given yet are not there. None once the job ended.

def chunk_states(self, job_id: int) -> bytes | None:
    """A byte per chunk of the job, in the order its source gave them: `PENDING_CHUNK`,

wait(job_id: int, timeout: float | None = None) -> JobSnapshot

Block until the job is terminal and its callbacks have run, or timeout passes.

Source code in src/ms_flow/engine/engine.py 
def wait(self, job_id: int, timeout: float | None = None) -> JobSnapshot:
    """Block until the job is terminal and its callbacks have run, or `timeout` passes."""
    job = self._jobs.get(job_id)
    if job is None:
        return self._ended[job_id]
    job.finished.wait(timeout)
    return job.snapshot()

items.title: close
items.text:
close() -> None

Interrupt what is running, let pending callbacks finish and stop the executors.

Source code in src/ms_flow/engine/engine.py 
def close(self) -> None:
    """Interrupt what is running, let pending callbacks finish and stop the executors."""
    if self._closed:
        return
    self._closed = True
    self._events.put((self._on_close,))
    self._events.put(None)
    self._threads[0].join()
    self._deliveries.put(None)
    self._threads[1].join()
    while not self._events.empty():  # what the last callbacks took, with the loop gone
        event = self._events.get()
        if event is not None and event[0] == self._on_delivered:
            event[0](*event[1:])
    for slot in self._executors.values():
        slot.impl.shutdown()
    for journal in self._journals.values():
        journal.close()
    if self._lock is not None:
        self._lock.close()

items.title: RayExecutor
items.text:
RayExecutor(address: str | None = None, capacity: int | None = None, shared: bool | None = None, names: dict | None = None, **init)

Tasks on a Ray cluster, which shares out its own CPUs, GPUs and memory.

address=None starts a cluster on this machine and stops it at shutdown; "auto" or host:port joins one that is running, on this machine or on others. What ray.init takes goes through. The functions and what they import have to be installed on every node.

shared says that every node sees the disk of this machine, as a cluster started here does. Without it each File of an element goes once to Ray's object store and a node keeps its copy in its temporary directory, and what a result names under a Dir comes back with it.

names takes each node's hostname to the name its tasks are shown under in hosts; without it the nodes are not asked where they are.

Source code in src/ms_flow/engine/executors.py 
def __init__(self, address: str | None = None, capacity: int | None = None, shared: bool | None = None,
             names: dict | None = None, **init):
    import ray

    self._ray, self.shared = ray, address is None if shared is None else shared
    # (path, when it changed, size) -> _Carried, for as long as a task that reads it is with
    # Ray: after the last one nothing holds it and the object store lets it go.
    self._carried = weakref.WeakValueDictionary()
    self._flying, self._killed = set(), set()  # the tasks Ray has, and those of them `kill` stopped
    # How far each watched task is: the nodes tell an actor, and what it holds is asked for
    # whenever `progress` is, so that one answers with what the time before brought.
    # `_watched` holds every task that tells the tally something, by its index: (owner, tag),
    # `owner` None for one that only says where it runs.
    self._tally, self._watched, self._said, self._asking = None, {}, {}, False
    self._names, self._at = names, {}  # hostname -> shown name; index -> hostname, as told
    self._ids = itertools.count()
    # What Ray starts on this machine dies with the thread that started it: this one stays
    # until `shutdown`, so whoever makes the executor may do it from a thread that ends.
    self._over, started, failed = threading.Event(), threading.Event(), []

    def keep():
        try:
            ray.init(address=address, **{"include_dashboard": False, "log_to_driver": False, **init})
        except BaseException as error:  # raised below, in the thread that asked
            failed.append(error)
            return
        finally:
            started.set()
        self._over.wait()

    threading.Thread(target=keep, name="msflow-ray", daemon=True).start()
    started.wait()
    if failed:
        raise failed[0]
    # How many tasks are handed to Ray at once: it queues those it has no room for.
    self.capacity = capacity or int(ray.cluster_resources().get("CPU", 1))
    self._lost = (ray.exceptions.WorkerCrashedError, ray.exceptions.NodeDiedError,
                  ray.exceptions.ObjectLostError, ray.exceptions.OutOfMemoryError)
    # max_retries=0: the engine is the one that runs a chunk again
    self._run = ray.remote(max_retries=0)(_apply if self.shared else _apply_far)
    self._sized = {}  # cost -> `_run` asking Ray for that much

items.title: submit
items.text:
submit(job, params=None, *, executor: str = 'process', batch: int | None = None, cpu: float | None = None, thread: bool | None = None, after=(), on_terminal=None, **engine) -> int

Start job and return its id. batch, cpu and thread override the task's; after adds jobs to wait for.

What else Engine.submit takes (key, journal, priority, total...) passes through. The sink is written on the engine's delivery thread, one transaction for each group of results, and an element is done once its rows are in. A job that goes to a journal always has a key, its own or one made here, and is recorded with what it was submitted with: see resume.

Source code in src/ms_flow/engine/flow.py 
def submit(self, job, params=None, *, executor: str = "process", batch: int | None = None,
           cpu: float | None = None, thread: bool | None = None, after=(), on_terminal=None, **engine) -> int:
    """Start `job` and return its id. `batch`, `cpu` and `thread` override the task's; `after`
    adds jobs to wait for.

    What else `Engine.submit` takes (`key`, `journal`, `priority`, `total`...) passes through.
    The sink is written on the engine's delivery thread, one transaction for each group of
    results, and an element is done once its rows are in.
    A job that goes to a journal always has a key, its own or one made here, and is recorded
    with what it was submitted with: see `resume`.
    """
    spec = job.__job__
    fn, output = spec["task"], spec["output"]
    # How many elements to a task: whoever submits, then the executor (a job in a queue takes
    # what its settings say), then the author of the task.
    own = getattr(self.engine.executor(executor), "batch", None)
    needs = {**fn.__task__, "batch": batch or own or fn.__task__["batch"], "cpu": cpu or fn.__task__["cpu"],
             "thread": fn.__task__.get("thread", False) if thread is None else thread}
    if spec["params_model"] is not None:
        params = spec["params_model"].model_validate(params or {})
    if engine.get("journal") is not None:
        engine["key"] = engine.get("key") or uuid.uuid4().hex
        engine["origin"] = _origin(job, params, {"executor": executor, "batch": batch, "cpu": cpu, "thread": thread, **{
            name: value for name, value in engine.items() if name not in ("journal", "key")}})
    if "params" in inspect.signature(fn).parameters:
        fn = functools.partial(fn, params=params)  # pickled with the function: once for each batch

    writer = None if output is None else _writer(output, params, self.project)

    def write(pairs):
        results = [result for _, result in pairs if result]
        if results:
            writer.write(results)

    def ended(snapshot):
        with self._lock:
            self._writing.pop(snapshot.id, None)
        try:
            if spec["finalize"] is not None:
                spec["finalize"](params, self.project, snapshot)
        finally:
            if on_terminal is not None:
                on_terminal(snapshot)

    source = job(params, self.project)
    reads = spec["reads"] | frozenset(getattr(source, "reads", ()))
    with self._lock:  # so `ended` cannot run before the job is in `_writing`
        after = [*after, *(job_id for job_id, tables in self._writing.items() if tables & reads)]
        job_id = self.engine.submit(executor, fn, source, name=spec["name"], after=after,
                                    on_results=write if writer is not None else None,
                                    on_finish=getattr(writer, "finish", None), on_terminal=ended,
                                    **needs, **engine)
        self._writing[job_id] = frozenset(getattr(writer, "tables", ()))
    return job_id

What the job recorded as key in journal was submitted with: job (as named reads it), params and options.

def origin(self, key: str, journal: str) -> dict:
    """What the job recorded as `key` in `journal` was submitted with: `job` (as `named` reads
    it), `params` and `options`."""
    spec = next((row["spec"] for row in self.engine.recorded(journal) if row["job_id"] == key), None)
    origin = json.loads(spec or "{}").get("origin")
    if origin is None:
        raise ValueError(f"job {key!r} is not on record with what it takes to submit it again: "
                         "its function has to be importable and its params JSON")
    return origin

items.title: resume
items.text:
resume(key: str, *, journal: str, **options) -> int

Submit again the job recorded as key in journal, with what it was submitted with: one that was interrupted or canceled continues. options say otherwise for this run, and bring what a record cannot keep (on_terminal, after).

Source code in src/ms_flow/engine/flow.py 
def resume(self, key: str, *, journal: str, **options) -> int:
    """Submit again the job recorded as `key` in `journal`, with what it was submitted with:
    one that was interrupted or canceled continues. `options` say otherwise for this run,
    and bring what a record cannot keep (`on_terminal`, `after`)."""
    origin = self.origin(key, journal)
    return self.submit(named(origin["job"]), origin["params"], key=key, journal=journal,
                       **{**origin["options"], **options})

items.title: A task and a job
items.text:
A task is a function marked with @task. It takes one element and returns its result; it takes params too when it names it.

from ms_flow import task


@task(cpu=1, retries=1, label="mol-{id}")
def weigh(molecule: dict, params) -> dict:
    return {"molecule_id": molecule["id"], "atoms": len(molecule["smiles"]) * params["scale"]}
Argument What it is cpu=, gpu=, mem_mb= What one element needs; the engine admits no more than the machine has retries= How many times a failed element runs again label= What an element goes by in the monitor and in a failure: a template its keys fill, or a function batch=, batched= How many elements travel together; with batched the function takes the list and returns one result for each thread= The function only waits for a program it starts: it runs on a thread and no worker is kept for it

A job is a function (params, project) marked with @job. It gives the elements, and names the task that takes them and where the results go.

from ms_flow import job, table_sink
from ms_flow.query import QuerySpec, Rows


@job(task=weigh, output=table_sink("weights", columns=("molecule_id", "atoms")))
def weigh_all(params, project):
    return Rows(project, QuerySpec(table="molecules", fields=("id", "smiles")))

The source is a generator, or anything read one element at a time. Rows reads a table of the project in pages, gives the job its total, and stops at the rows the table had when the job started. params is what submit was given, None when nothing was; params_model= validates it with a pydantic model.

Tasks and jobs live in a module the workers can import, never in __main__.

items.title: Running a job
items.text:
A Workspace keeps the projects of an app and runs jobs in the active one.

from ms_flow import Workspace

ms = Workspace(app_id="demo")
ms.create_or_open_project(name="demo", folder="./demo_project", activate=True)

job_id = ms.submit(weigh_all, {"scale": 2})
snapshot = ms.engine.wait(job_id)
print(snapshot.status, snapshot.chunks_done, snapshot.chunks_total)   # completed 200 200
ms.shutdown()
  • submit returns at once. ms.engine.status(job_id) and ms.engine.wait(job_id) return a JobSnapshot.
  • executor= says where the job runs: local (the pool of processes of this machine, the default), thread, or another active executor.
  • batch=, cpu= and thread= override the task's; after= names jobs to wait for. A job also waits for the jobs that write the tables it reads.
  • ms.engine.cancel(job_id) stops a job.

items.title: Where the results go
Following a job
items.text:
Call What it gives ms.engine.status(job_id) JobSnapshot: status, chunks_done, chunks_failed, chunks_total, progress, tasks_running, cpu_used, error, key... ms.jobs() Every job of the active project, earlier sessions too, read from its journal; safe to poll ms.job_tasks(job_id) The tasks in flight of a job of this session ms.job_failures(key) The elements that failed: attempt, error (the traceback) and input

A job ends completed, completed_with_errors (some elements failed), failed, canceled or interrupted. A task tells how far it is on its element with report(fraction); the snapshot's progress counts it.

items.title: Continuing a job
items.text:
Every job of a project is recorded in its journal (executor.db) under a key: the one given with key=, or one made for it.

  • Closing the project, or the app, interrupts its jobs.
  • ms.resume(key) submits the job again with what it was submitted with.
  • A job that was interrupted or canceled continues: the elements it had done are recognised by their own keys and not run again.
job_id = ms.submit(weigh_all, {"scale": 1}, key="weigh")
...
ms.engine.cancel(job_id)          # canceled with 68 of 200 done
ms.engine.wait(ms.resume("weigh"))  # completed: the other 132 ran

An element is recognised by content_key(element), or by the _key of a dict element. Results written by an element that was running when the job stopped may be written again when it continues: write them so that a second write changes nothing (a conflict key, or skipping what is there).

ms.engine.discard("project", key) gives a recorded job up.

items.title: Where jobs run
items.text:
Machines are kept as hosts, and who runs jobs on them as executors, by name, in the settings of ~/.molsuite ($MOLSUITE_HOME moves it).

Executor kind What it is loky The pool of processes of this machine: local ray A Ray cluster started from this machine over its hosts; without local among them this machine runs none of its tasks queue The queue of an HPC (slurm), its host the login node 
ms.save_host("lab", address="me@lab-server", cpus=32)      # as `ssh` knows it
ms.save_executor("lab-ray", kind="ray", hosts=["local", "lab"])
ms.activate("lab-ray")                     # starts it; jobs go to it by name
ms.submit(weigh_all, {"scale": 2}, executor="lab-ray")
ms.move(key, "local")                      # a job that runs continues elsewhere
  • Commands go over the system's ssh, through ms_env: keys and users come from ~/.ssh/config, no credential is handled.
  • Give each host an address that does not change: a name (ssh resolves it from ~/.ssh/config, DNS or mDNS, such as lab-server.local) or a fixed IP (a DHCP reservation in the router). An address the network gives anew each time makes the host unreachable the next time its machine joins.
  • A Ray cluster takes only the machines on the network of the first host: each one joins the address of this machine as that host sees it.
  • A host with no env is given the environment of the app by the app (Workspace.host_env).
  • ms.executors() lists them with their state; deactivate stops one.

items.title: The engine without a project
items.text:
ms_flow.engine.Engine runs a function on every element of an iterable, with no project and no journal.

from ms_flow.engine import Engine, ProcessExecutor
from workers import square_of

with Engine(cpus=4) as engine:
    engine.register("process", ProcessExecutor(4))
    results = {}
    job_id = engine.submit("process", square_of, range(100),
                           on_result=lambda key, result: results.update({key: result}))
    engine.wait(job_id)

engine.attach(name, path) gives it a journal, and journal= and key= in submit record a job there. Flow(engine, project) runs @jobs with it.

items.title: Payloads
items.text:
A payload is the bytes of one entity: an SDF, a PDBQT, a pose. Payloads live in append-only volume files under volumes/, next to project.db. The ms_payloads table says where each one is. Your tables keep only an id:

CREATE TABLE ligands (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    structure_payload_id INTEGER REFERENCES ms_payloads(id)
);

ms_flow never needs your schema. It finds the columns that hold payload ids by their REFERENCES ms_payloads(id) foreign key. Moving bytes, for example when compacting, rewrites ms_payloads and never your tables. A payload id never changes.

items.title: Write payloads from a job
items.text:
A task returns Payload objects in place of ids. The sink stores the bytes and writes the ids, in the same transaction as the rows:

from ms_flow.engine import job, task
from ms_flow.payloads import Payload
from ms_flow.sinks import table_sink


@task()
def prepare(name: str) -> dict:
    sdf = build_sdf(name)  # your code
    return {"name": name, "structure_payload_id": Payload(sdf, kind="sdf", series="ligands")}


@job(task=prepare, output=table_sink("ligands", columns=("name", "structure_payload_id")))
def import_ligands(params, project):
    yield from params["names"]

graph_sink works the same way, in any node.

  • series groups payloads with the same lifetime, so they share volumes and compact well together. Use one series per kind of data ("ligands", "poses").
  • codec is "zstd" (the default), "zlib" or "none". Use "none" for data that is already compressed.
  • The payload is compressed when it is pickled, so the compression happens in the worker. The process that owns the project only appends bytes.

When the sink commits, the bytes are already on disk (fdatasync). A crash never leaves a row that points to missing bytes.

items.title: Compression dictionaries
items.text:
A zstd dictionary trained on a series compresses small records much better: 5.9× against 4.3× without it on real SDF records. It is also faster. Train one when a series has enough payloads (10 000 are sampled across the whole series):

project.payloads.train_dictionary("ligands")

A job hands the dictionary to its tasks as a File. Executors without the project's disk carry it once per job:

@task()
def prepare(element: dict) -> dict:
    sdf = build_sdf(element["name"])
    return {"name": element["name"], "structure_payload_id":
            Payload(sdf, series="ligands", dictionary=element["dictionary"])}


@job(task=prepare, output=table_sink("ligands", columns=("name", "structure_payload_id")))
def import_ligands(params, project):
    dictionary = project.payloads.dictionary("ligands")  # None until one is trained
    return [{"name": name, "dictionary": dictionary} for name in params["names"]]

The dictionary id travels inside each zstd frame, so reading needs nothing else. Payloads compressed with an older dictionary stay readable. Compaction moves them to the series' current dictionary.

items.title: Read payloads
items.text:
store = project.payloads
data = store.get(payload_id)            # bytes
found = store.get_many(ids)             # {id: bytes}, read in disk order
for payload_id, data in store.iter_bytes(ids):  # bounded memory, for exports
    ...

A job whose tasks need the bytes uses with_payloads as its source. Each row gets the bytes of its payload under the key you name, so a task never sees a path:

from ms_flow.payloads import with_payloads
from ms_flow.query import QuerySpec, Rows


@job(task=dock, output=...)
def docking(params, project):
    rows = Rows(project, QuerySpec(table="ligands"))
    return with_payloads(project, rows, {"structure_payload_id": "structure"})

Rows are read 500 at a time in disk order, so memory stays bounded however big the table is. A program that only reads paths gets a file in two ways:

  • store.materialize(payload_id, directory, suffix) writes the payload once and returns it as a File. Use it for a receptor shared by every task.
  • scratch_file(data, suffix) is a context manager. It gives a temporary file (in /dev/shm when it has room) and deletes it on leaving.

Corrupt or missing bytes raise PayloadCorrupt, which carries the payload id.

items.title: Delete payloads
items.text:
Delete your rows, then release the payload ids they held:

with sqlite3.connect(project.db_path) as conn:
    ids = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
        "DELETE FROM ligands WHERE name LIKE 'tmp%' RETURNING structure_payload_id")]
project.payloads.release(ids)

release only drops payloads that no foreign key references, so releasing an id still in use does nothing. A volume left with no live payload is deleted at once, without copying anything.

items.title: Maintenance
items.text:
Call What it does check(full=False) Returns a Report: missing volumes, references past a file's end, unreferenced payloads, empty volumes, dead share per volume, missing dictionaries, orphan files. full=True also reads and verifies every payload. report.ok means every referenced payload is readable; report.clean also means there is nothing to clean up. compact(min_dead=0.5, order_by=None) Copies the live payloads of sealed volumes that are at least half dead (or small) into new volumes, then deletes the old ones. Ids do not change. order_by is SQL that returns payload ids in the order you want them next to each other on disk (SELECT structure_payload_id FROM ligands ORDER BY score). repair() Clears what crashes leave behind: unreferenced payloads, orphan volume files, empty volumes. Never deletes a referenced payload. Returns a new check().

Compaction can run while other processes read. A reader whose volume disappears reads the new location of the payload. To order compaction with your other jobs, submit it as a job:

from ms_flow.payloads import compaction

flow.submit(compaction())

The compaction job waits for jobs writing payloads to finish, and jobs reading payloads wait for it.

On a 100 000-molecule project (225 MB stored), a cold check(full=True) takes 4.3 s. Compaction copies live data at about 34 MB/s, limited by the disk.

items.title: payloads
items.text:
Per-entity payloads in append-only volumes.

The bytes of each entity (an SDF, a PDBQT, a pose) live in volumes/<id:09d>.vol next to project.db; a row of ms_payloads says where. Apps keep only <role>_payload_id INTEGER REFERENCES ms_payloads(id): moving bytes rewrites ms_payloads and never an app table, and ms_flow never needs the app schema.

Volume: a 32-byte header (MSVOL, version, volume id, series), then needles. Needle: a 16-byte header (crc32, stored length, raw length, codec, flags), then the bytes. A volume has one writer and only grows; a sealed volume never changes.

Each payload says its codec (none, zlib, zstd), so volumes mix them. A Payload compresses itself when it is pickled, i.e. in the worker that made it: the writer only appends bytes. A PayloadGroup stores several payloads as one needle, which compresses them better (the poses of one docking, about half); each part keeps its own row and id, with its place in the needle's raw bytes (part_offset, part_length). A zstd frame names its dictionary (dicts/<id>.zdict, trained per series with PayloadStore.train_dictionary), so reading needs no table.

Maintenance: check reports, release drops payloads nobody references, compact copies the live needles of mostly dead volumes to new ones (recompressing them with the series' current dictionary) and repair clears what crashes leave. Ids never change: compacting rewrites the location of a row, with compare-and-set (I6).

POSIX only (pread/pwritev). Nothing here imports SQL at module level: tasks import Payload in workers.

def packed(self) -> Payload:

Store payloads inside the caller's transaction; return their ids, in order: one per Payload, one per part of a PayloadGroup (an empty group stores nothing).

The bytes are on disk (fdatasync) when this returns, so the caller's commit never points to lost bytes. If that transaction does not commit, the volumes go back to the size they had before it.

Source code in src/ms_flow/payloads.py 
def put(self, session: Any, payloads: Iterable[Payload | PayloadGroup]) -> list[int]:
    """Store `payloads` inside the caller's transaction; return their ids, in order: one per
    `Payload`, one per part of a `PayloadGroup` (an empty group stores nothing).

    The bytes are on disk (fdatasync) when this returns, so the caller's commit never
    points to lost bytes. If that transaction does not commit, the volumes go back to
    the size they had before it.
    """
    payloads = list(payloads)
    if not payloads:
        return []
    connection = session.connection()  # begins the caller's transaction
    tx = self._transaction(session)
    cursor = connection.connection.dbapi_connection.cursor()
    try:
        pending: dict[_Volume, list] = {}
        placed = []
        for payload in payloads:
            sizes = None
            if isinstance(payload, PayloadGroup):
                payload, sizes = payload.packed()
                if not sizes:
                    continue
            payload = payload.packed()  # done already when it came from a worker
            data, codec = payload.data, CODECS[payload.codec]
            size = len(data)
            volume = self._volume_for(tx, cursor, payload.series, NEEDLE + size)
            crc = zlib.crc32(data)
            pending.setdefault(volume, [volume.end, []])[1] += (
                _NEEDLE.pack(crc, size, payload.raw_length, codec, 0),
                data,
            )
            row = (volume.id, volume.end, size, payload.raw_length, codec, crc, payload.kind)
            if sizes is None:
                placed.append((*row, None, None))
            else:
                placed += [(*row, start, length) for start, length in zip(accumulate(sizes, initial=0), sizes)]
            volume.end += NEEDLE + size
        for volume, (offset, buffers) in pending.items():
            try:
                _write_all(volume.fd, buffers, offset)
            except OSError as error:  # a full disk: the caller's rollback cuts what got in
                raise OSError(error.errno, f"cannot write payloads to {self.path(volume.id)}: "
                                           f"{error.strerror}") from error
        _fault("appended")
        for volume in pending:
            _datasync(volume.fd)
            cursor.execute("UPDATE ms_volumes SET size = ? WHERE id = ?", (volume.end, volume.id))
        if tx.dir_dirty:  # a new volume file must survive a crash too
            _fsync_dir(self.directory)
            tx.dir_dirty = False
        _fault("synced")
        ids = []
        for row in placed:
            cursor.execute(
                'INSERT INTO ms_payloads (volume_id, "offset", length, raw_length, codec, crc32, kind,'
                " part_offset, part_length) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                row,
            )
            ids.append(cursor.lastrowid)
        return ids
    finally:
        cursor.close()

def referencing_columns(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(table, column) of every app column that holds payload ids.

    Read from the schema (`PRAGMA foreign_key_list`): an app declares
    `REFERENCES ms_payloads(id)` and registers nothing with ms_flow.
    """
    with self.engine.connect() as conn:
        tables = [r[0] for r in conn.exec_driver_sql("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table'")]
        return [
            (table, fk[3])
            for table in tables
            for fk in conn.exec_driver_sql(f'PRAGMA foreign_key_list("{table}")')
            if fk[2] == "ms_payloads"
        ]

def get_many(self, ids: Iterable[int]) -> dict[int, bytes]:
    """Bytes by id. Read in (volume, offset) order; unknown ids raise KeyError."""
    wanted = list(dict.fromkeys(int(i) for i in ids))
    located = self._locate(wanted)
    missing = [i for i in wanted if i not in located]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown payload ids: {missing[:10]}")
    found, needle, raw = {}, None, b""
    for i in sorted(located, key=lambda i: located[i][:2]):
        location = located[i]
        if location[:2] != needle:  # the parts of a group: one read, one decompression
            needle, raw = location[:2], self._read(i, location)
        found[i] = _part(raw, location)
    return found

def materialize(self, payload_id: int, directory: str | os.PathLike, suffix: str | None = None):
    """The payload as the file `<directory>/<id><suffix>`, written once: what a job hands its
    tasks as a `File` (a receptor), which executors without the disk carry once per job.
    Without `suffix`, the payload's kind is the extension (`.pdbqt`)."""
    from ms_flow.engine.files import File

    if suffix is None:
        kind = self.kinds([payload_id]).get(int(payload_id))
        suffix = f".{kind}" if kind else ""
    path = Path(directory) / f"{int(payload_id)}{suffix}"
    if not path.exists():
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        part = path.with_name(f".{path.name}.{os.getpid()}.{threading.get_ident()}")
        part.write_bytes(self.get(payload_id))
        os.replace(part, path)
    return File(path)

def train_dictionary(self, series: str, samples: int = DICT_SAMPLES, size: int = DICT_SIZE):
    """Train a zstd dictionary on `samples` payloads spread over `series` (the head of a
    library is not like the rest of it) and make it the series' current one: a `File`."""
    import random

    from ms_flow.engine.files import File

    with self.engine.connect() as conn:
        ids = [r[0] for r in conn.exec_driver_sql(
            "SELECT p.id FROM ms_payloads p JOIN ms_volumes v ON v.id = p.volume_id WHERE v.series = ?",
            (series,))]
    if len(ids) < 100:
        raise ValueError(f"series {series!r} has {len(ids)} payloads; a dictionary needs a few thousand")
    picked = sorted(random.Random(0).sample(ids, min(samples, len(ids))))
    data = [b for _, b in self.iter_bytes(picked)]
    with self.engine.begin() as conn:
        dict_id = conn.exec_driver_sql(
            "INSERT INTO ms_payload_dicts (series, samples) VALUES (?, ?)",
            (series, len(data))).lastrowid
        trained = _zstd().train_dictionary(size, data, dict_id=dict_id)
        path = self.directory / "dicts" / f"{dict_id}.zdict"
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        part = path.with_name(path.name + ".part")
        with open(part, "wb") as file:
            file.write(trained.as_bytes())
            file.flush()
            os.fsync(file.fileno())
        os.replace(part, path)
        _fsync_dir(path.parent)
    return File(path)

def check(self, full: bool = False) -> Report:
    """What is wrong or left over; `full` also reads every needle (crc32, codec, dictionary)."""
    report = Report()
    with self.engine.connect() as conn:
        volumes = {r[0]: r[1:] for r in conn.exec_driver_sql("SELECT id, state, size FROM ms_volumes")}
        stats = {r[0]: r[1:] for r in conn.exec_driver_sql(
            f'SELECT volume_id, sum({NEEDLE} + length), max("offset" + {NEEDLE} + length)'
            f" FROM {_NEEDLES} GROUP BY volume_id")}
        report.unreferenced = [r[0] for r in conn.exec_driver_sql(
            f"SELECT id FROM ms_payloads WHERE {self._unreferenced()}")]
        dicts = [r[0] for r in conn.exec_driver_sql("SELECT id FROM ms_payload_dicts")]
    short = {}  # volume id -> its size on disk, when rows point past it
    for volume_id, (state, size) in volumes.items():
        live, end = stats.get(volume_id, (0, HEADER))
        try:
            on_disk = self.path(volume_id).stat().st_size
        except FileNotFoundError:
            if volume_id in stats:
                report.missing_volumes.append(volume_id)
            continue
        if state == "trash" or (state == "sealed" and volume_id not in stats):
            report.empty.append(volume_id)
        elif state == "sealed":
            report.dead[volume_id] = round(1 - live / max(size - HEADER, 1), 4)
        if end > on_disk:
            short[volume_id] = on_disk
    with self.engine.connect() as conn:
        for volume_id in report.missing_volumes:
            for (pid,) in conn.exec_driver_sql("SELECT id FROM ms_payloads WHERE volume_id = ?", (volume_id,)):
                report.broken[pid] = f"volume {volume_id} is missing"
        for volume_id, on_disk in short.items():
            for (pid,) in conn.exec_driver_sql(
                    f'SELECT id FROM ms_payloads WHERE volume_id = ? AND "offset" + {NEEDLE} + length > ?',
                    (volume_id, on_disk)):
                report.broken[pid] = f"past the end of volume {volume_id}"
        if full:
            rows = conn.exec_driver_sql('SELECT id, volume_id, "offset", length, raw_length, codec, crc32'
                                        ' FROM ms_payloads ORDER BY volume_id, "offset"')
            needle, error = None, None
            for pid, *location in rows:
                if tuple(location[:2]) != needle:  # the parts of a group: read once
                    needle, error = tuple(location[:2]), None
                    try:
                        self._read(pid, tuple(location))
                    except Exception as failure:  # a report: whatever stops a read goes in it
                        error = str(failure)
                if error is not None and pid not in report.broken:
                    report.broken[pid] = error
    report.missing_dicts = [d for d in dicts if not (self.directory / "dicts" / f"{d}.zdict").exists()]
    known = set(volumes)
    report.orphans = sorted(volume_id for volume_id in self._volume_files()
                            if volume_id not in known and self._unowned(volume_id))
    return report

def release(self, ids: Iterable[int]) -> int:
    """Delete the payload rows of `ids` that no app row references (after the app deleted its
    rows); a sealed volume left without rows goes, unread. Returns how many rows went."""
    ids = list(dict.fromkeys(int(i) for i in ids))
    guard = self._unreferenced()
    released = 0
    with self.engine.begin() as conn:
        for start in range(0, len(ids), LOCATE_CHUNK):
            chunk = ids[start : start + LOCATE_CHUNK]
            released += conn.exec_driver_sql(
                f"DELETE FROM ms_payloads WHERE id IN ({','.join('?' * len(chunk))}) AND {guard}",
                tuple(chunk)).rowcount
        self._trash_empty(conn)
    self._empty_trash()
    return released

def compact(self, min_dead: float = 0.5, small: int | None = None, order_by: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Copy the live needles of sealed volumes with at least `min_dead` dead bytes (or of two or
    more volumes of a series under `small` bytes, a quarter of VOLUME_SIZE by default) to new volumes, move their rows there and
    delete the old ones. Needles are recompressed with the series' current dictionary.

    `order_by` is SQL that gives payload ids in the order wanted next to each other on disk
    (`SELECT current_payload_id FROM molecules ORDER BY score`); the rest keep theirs.
    Never touches an active volume, so it can run next to writers and readers (I6, I7).
    """
    small = VOLUME_SIZE // 4 if small is None else small
    self._empty_trash()
    with self.engine.connect() as conn:
        rows = conn.exec_driver_sql(
            f"SELECT v.id, v.series, v.size, coalesce(sum({NEEDLE} + p.length), 0) FROM ms_volumes v"
            f" LEFT JOIN {_NEEDLES} p ON p.volume_id = v.id WHERE v.state = 'sealed' GROUP BY v.id").fetchall()
    picked: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
    for series in {r[1] for r in rows}:
        mine = [(vid, 1 - live / max(size - HEADER, 1), size) for vid, s, size, live in rows if s == series]
        chosen = [vid for vid, dead, _ in mine if dead >= min_dead]
        smalls = [vid for vid, dead, size in mine if dead < min_dead and size < small]
        chosen += smalls if len(smalls) > 1 else []  # one small volume alone gains nothing
        if chosen:
            picked[series] = chosen
    stats = {"volumes": 0, "moved": 0, "read_mb": 0.0, "written_mb": 0.0}
    for series, volume_ids in picked.items():
        self._compact_series(series, volume_ids, order_by, stats)
    self._empty_trash()
    return stats

def repair(self, report: Report | None = None) -> Report:
    """Clear what `check` reports as garbage: cut the tails of dead writers, delete unreferenced
    rows, empty volumes and orphan files. A referenced row is never deleted. Returns a new check."""
    report = report or self.check()
    self._recover()
    self.release(report.unreferenced)
    for volume_id in report.orphans:
        if self._unowned(volume_id):
            self.path(volume_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    with self.engine.begin() as conn:
        self._trash_empty(conn)
    self._empty_trash()
    return self.check()

def close(self) -> None:
    """Close files. Call it with no transaction of this store open."""
    with self._lock:
        volumes = [v for free in self._free.values() for v in free]
        self._free.clear()
    for volume in volumes:
        os.close(volume.fd)
    with self._fd_lock:
        for entry in self._fds.values():
            entry[2] = True
            if entry[1] == 0:
                os.close(entry[0])
        self._fds.clear()

def with_payloads(project: Any, rows: Iterable[dict], fields: dict[str, str], window: int = READ_WINDOW,
                  kinds: bool = False):
    """A job's source whose rows carry the bytes of their payloads, so a task gets bytes and never a path.

    `fields` maps an id column to the key that gets its bytes (`{"current_payload_id": "ligand"}`;
    a NULL id gives `None`). Rows are read `window` at a time in (volume, offset) order, so at most
    that many hold bytes here, and the engine reads only its window ahead (I8). What `rows` knows
    (`open`, `remaining`, `reads` of `ms_flow.query.Rows`) passes through. With `kinds`, each key
    also gets `<key>_kind`, the kind its payload was stored with, so a task knows how to parse it.
    """
    from ms_flow.core.database import resolve_project_store

    return _WithPayloads(resolve_project_store(project).payloads, rows, fields, window, kinds)

def compaction(min_dead: float = 0.5, order_by: str | None = None):
    """`PayloadStore.compact` as a job of ms_flow, `flow.submit(compaction())`: it waits for the
    jobs writing payloads (every table writer says it writes `ms_payloads`), and a job reading
    `ms_payloads` or `ms_volumes` waits for it. It runs in the process that owns the project (I4)."""
    from ms_flow.engine.flow import job, task

    class Compactor:
        tables = ("ms_payloads", "ms_volumes")

        def __init__(self, params, project):
            from ms_flow.core.database import resolve_project_store

            self.store = resolve_project_store(project).payloads

        def write(self, results):
            pass

        def finish(self):
            self.stats = self.store.compact(min_dead, order_by=order_by)

    @task(thread=True)
    def nothing(element):
        return None

    return job(task=nothing, name="compact payloads", output=Compactor, reads=("ms_payloads",))(
        lambda params, project: [None])

@contextmanager
def scratch_file(data: bytes, suffix: str = ""):
    """`data` as a temporary file, for a program that only reads paths: in /dev/shm when it is
    there and has room for it, in the system's temporary folder if not. Deleted on leaving."""
    directory = None
    if os.path.isdir("/dev/shm") and os.access("/dev/shm", os.W_OK):
        if shutil.disk_usage("/dev/shm").free > 2 * len(data):  # ponytail: room now, not while it is written
            directory = "/dev/shm"
    fd, name = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=suffix, prefix="msflow-", dir=directory)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as file:
            file.write(data)
        yield Path(name)
    finally:
        with suppress(FileNotFoundError):
            os.unlink(name)
